01
Before the first verse · Vol. 4, p. 455

Opening of the surah

Vol. 4, p. 455
Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa is Meccan [except for verses 81 and 82, which are Medinan]; it has 96 verses, and it is said 97 [revealed after Ṭā Hā]. In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.
سورة الواقعة مكية [إلا آيتي 81 و 82 فمدنيتان] وآياتها 96 وقيل 97 آية [نزلت بعد طه] بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ
02
Q 56:1–7 · Vol. 4, pp. 455–456

Verses 1 to 7

The verses as the commentary quotes them
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. When the Event occurs (1), there is no denying its occurrence (2), lowering, raising (3). When the earth is shaken violently (4) and the mountains are crumbled to bits (5) and become scattered dust (6), and you will be three kinds (7)
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم إِذا وَقَعَتِ الْواقِعَةُ (1) لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِها كاذِبَةٌ (2) خافِضَةٌ رافِعَةٌ (3) إِذا رُجَّتِ الْأَرْضُ رَجًّا (4) وَبُسَّتِ الْجِبالُ بَسًّا (5) فَكانَتْ هَباءً مُنْبَثًّا (6) وَكُنْتُمْ أَزْواجاً ثَلاثَةً (7)
Vol. 4, p. 455
. “When the Event occurs” is like your saying: the thing that was to be came to be, and the happening happened; and what is meant is the Resurrection: it is described as occurring because it will certainly occur, as if it were said: when that which must occur occurs. The occurrence of a matter is its descent. One says: what I was expecting occurred, that is, what I was awaiting descended.
وَقَعَتِ الْواقِعَةُ كقولك: كانت الكائنة، وحدثت الحادثة، والمراد القيامة: وصفت بالوقوع لأنها تقع لا محالة، فكأنه قيل: إذا وقعت التي لا بدّ من وقوعها، ووقوع الأمر: نزوله. يقال: وقع ما كنت أتوقعه، أى: نزل ما كنت أترقب نزوله.
Question
If you ask: What governs the accusative of idhā?
فإن قلت: بم انتصب إذا؟
Answer
I answer: laysa, as in your saying “on Friday I have no work”; or an implied verb, meaning: when it occurs, such-and-such will be; or an implied “remember.” “Kādhiba” (a denier) is a lying soul, that is: when it occurs there will be no soul that lies about God and lies in denying the unseen, because every soul then will be believing, truthful and affirming, whereas most souls today are liars and deniers, as in His saying “So when they saw Our might they said: We believe in God alone,” and “those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it until the Hour comes upon them suddenly.” And the lām is like the one in His saying “O would that I had sent ahead for my life.” Or: it has no soul that denies it and says to it: you will not be, as many souls today deny it and tell it: you will not be. Or it is from their saying: kadhabat fulānan nafsuhu fī l-khaṭbi bi-ʿaẓīm, when his soul emboldened him to take on something great and said to him: you can bear it and more, so face it and do not mind it; in the sense that it is an event unbearable in its severity and horror, and that no soul then will tell its owner what it tells him at great matters and make attractive to him bearing it and having the strength for it, because they on that day are too weak and abject for that. Do you not see His saying “like scattered moths”? and the moth is a proverb for weakness. It is also said that kādhiba is a verbal noun like ʿāqiba, meaning denial, from your saying: ḥamala ʿalā qarnihi fa-mā kadhaba, that is, he did not shrink and was not deterred. And its reality:
قلت: بليس. كقولك يوم الجمعة ليس لي شغل. أو بمحذوف، يعنى: إذا وقعت كان كيت وكيت: أو بإضمار اذكر كاذِبَةٌ نفس كاذبة، أى: لا تكون حين تقع نفس تكذب على الله وتكذب في تكذيب الغيب، لأنّ كل نفس حينئذ مؤمنة صادقة مصدّقة، وأكثر النفوس اليوم كواذب مكذبات، كقوله تعالى فَلَمَّا رَأَوْا بَأْسَنا قالُوا آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَحْدَهُ، لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ حَتَّى يَرَوُا الْعَذابَ الْأَلِيمَ، وَلا يَزالُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِنْهُ حَتَّى تَأْتِيَهُمُ السَّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً واللام مثلها في قوله تعالى يا لَيْتَنِي قَدَّمْتُ لِحَياتِي أو: ليس لها نفس تكذبها وتقول لها: لم تكوني كما لها اليوم نفوس كثيرة يكذبنها، يقلن لها: لن تكوني. أو هي من قولهم: كذبت فلانا نفسه في الخطب، بعظيم، إذا شجعته على مباشرته وقالت له: إنك تطيقه وما فوقه فتعرّض له ولا تبال به، على معنى: أنها وقعة لا تطاق شدّة وفظاعة. وأن لا نفس حينئذ تحدث صاحبها بما تحدثه به عند عظائم الأمور وتزين له احتمالها وإطاقتها، لأنهم يومئذ أضعف من ذلك وأذل. ألا ترى إلى قوله تعالى كَالْفَراشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ والفراش مثل في الضعف. وقيل كاذِبَةٌ مصدر كالعاقبة بمعنى التكذيب، من قولك: حمل على قرنه فما كذب، أى: فما جبن وما ثبط. وحقيقته:
Vol. 4, p. 456
he did not lie to his soul in what it told him, of his capacity for it and his advance upon it. Zuhayr said: “…………… when … the lion shrank from his peers, he was true” «1» — that is: when it occurs, it will have no turning back or retreat. “Lowering, raising”: it is lowering, raising; it raises some peoples and lowers others: either as a description of its severity, because great events are so — some people are raised in them to ranks and others abased; or because the wretched are lowered to the depths and the blessed raised to the degrees; or because it shakes things and removes them from their places, lowering some and raising others, when the sky falls in pieces and the stars scatter and are darkened and the mountains move, passing through the air as clouds pass. It is also read khāfiḍatan rāfiʿatan in the accusative as a circumstantial. “Rujjat”: moved violently until everything on it of mountain and building collapses; “and the mountains were crumbled” and pulverized «2» until they become like groats (sawīq), or driven, from bassa l-ghanam when one drives them, as in “and the mountains are set in motion.” “Munbathth”: scattered. It is also read with tāʾ, that is, cut off. It is also read ruja and busa, that is, shaken and gone. In the speech of the daughter of al-Khass «3»: “Her eye is sunken, her haunches quiver, and she walks with legs apart.”
فما كذب نفسه فيما حدثته به. من إطاقته له وإقدامه عليه. قال زهير: ............... .. إذا … ما اللّيث كذّب عن أقرانه صدقا «1» أى: إذا وقعت لم تكن لها رجعة ولا ارتداد خافِضَةٌ رافِعَةٌ على: هي خافضة رافعة، ترفع أقواما وتضع آخرين: إما وصفا لها بالشدّة، لأنّ الواقعات العظام كذلك: يرتفع فيها ناس إلى مراتب ويتضع ناس، وإما لأنّ الأشقياء يحطون إلى الدركات، والسعداء يرفعون إلى الدرجات، وإما أنها تزلزل الأشياء وتزيلها عن مقارّها، فتخفض بعضا وترفع بعضا: حيث تسقط السماء كسفا وتنتثر الكواكب وتنكدر وتسير الجبال فتمرّ في الجوّ مرّ السحاب، وقرئ: خافضة رافعة بالنصب على الحال رُجَّتِ حرّكت تحريكا شديدا حتى ينهدم كل شيء فوقها من جبل وبناء وَبُسَّتِ الْجِبالُ وفتت «2» حتى تعود كالسويق، أو سيقت من بس العنم إذا ساقها، كقوله وَسُيِّرَتِ الْجِبالُ، مُنْبَثًّا متفرقا. وقرئ بالتاء أى: منقطعا. وقرئ: رجت وبست، أى: ارتجت وذهبت. وفي كلام بنت الخس «3» : عينها هاج، وصلاها راج. وهي تمشى وتفاج.
Question
If you ask: What governs idhā rujjat?
فإن قلت: بم انتصب إذا رجت؟
Answer
I answer: it is a substitute for idhā waqaʿat. It can also be governed by khāfiḍa rāfiʿa, that is: it lowers and raises at the time of the shaking of the earth and the crumbling of the mountains, because at that time what is high is lowered and what is low is raised. “Azwāj”: kinds; the kinds, some together with others or mentioned together, are called azwāj.
قلت: هو بدل من إذا وقعت. ويجوز أن ينتصب بخافضة رافعة. أى: تخفض وترفع وقت رج الأرض، وبس الجبال لأنه عند ذلك ينخفض ما هو مرتفع ويرتفع ما هو منخفض أَزْواجاً أصنافا، يقال للأصناف التي بعضها مع بعض أو يذكر بعضها مع بعض: أزواج.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 456
1. (1) . A lion of ʿAthar hunts men, when
…. the lion shrinks from his peers, he is true. By Zuhayr, praising a brave man; he borrowed for him the name of the lion by explicit metaphor, and hunting is the embellishment. ʿAthar is the name of a place; that is, a brave man in ʿAthar who kills men when the mighty rider shrinks, that is, grows cowardly and weak toward his peers in battle — then he is true and his resolve is carried out and he kills his peer. In the verse is an antithesis between truthfulness and lying (ṣidq/kadhib), and it is among the beauties of speech.
2. . His statement «wa-futtitat until they become like groats»: the wording of al-Nasafī is: wa-futtitat (the intensive form). (ʿ)
3. . His statement «wa-fī kalām bint al-Khass»: in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: al-khass with fatḥa is a herb; al-khuss with ḍamma is the name of a man, and from it: Hind bint al-Khuss. ʿAyn hājja: that is, sunken. Al-ṣalā: what is on the right and left of the tail. Fajajtu mā bayna rijlayya afujjuhumā: when I spread them apart. One says: huwa yamshī mufājjan. (ʿ)
1. (1) . ليث يعثر يصطاد الرجال إذا
…. ما الليث كذب عن أقرانه صدقا لزهير يمدح شجاعا، فاستعار له اسم الأسد على طريق التصريحية، والاصطياد ترشيح. وعثر: اسم موضع، أى شجاع في عثر يقتل الرجال إذا كذب أى جبن وضعف الفارس الشديد عن أقرانه في الحرب، صدق هو ونفذ عزمه وقتل قرنه، وفي البيت الطباق بين الصدق والكذب، وهو من بديع الكلام.
2. . قوله «وفتت حتى تعود كالسويق» عبارة النسفي: وفتتت. (ع)
3. . قوله «وفي كلام بنت الخس» في الصحاح: الخس بالفتح: بقلة. والخس بالضم: اسم رجل. ومنه: هند بنت الخس. وعين هاجة: أى غائرة. والصلا: ما عن يمين الذنب ويساره. وفججت ما بين رجلي أفجهما: إذا فتحت. يقال: هو يمشى مفاجا. (ع)
03
Q 56:8–9 · Vol. 4, pp. 456–457

Verses 8 to 9

The verses as the commentary quotes them
So the companions of the right — what are the companions of the right (8)? And the companions of the left — what are the companions of the left (9)
فَأَصْحابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ ما أَصْحابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ (8) وَأَصْحابُ الْمَشْئَمَةِ ما أَصْحابُ الْمَشْئَمَةِ (9)
Vol. 4, p. 456
? “The companions of the right” are those given their records in their right hands; “and the companions of the left” are those given them in their left. Or: the people of the elevated station and the people of the low station, from your saying: so-and-so is to me on the right, so-and-so is to me on the left, when you describe them as high or low with you; and that is because of their taking the right as auspicious and the left as ill-omened,
فَأَصْحابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ الذين يؤتون صحائفهم بأيمانهم وَأَصْحابُ الْمَشْئَمَةِ الذين يؤتونها بشمائلهم. أو أصحاب المنزلة السنية وأصحاب المنزلة الدنية، من قولك: فلان منى باليمين، فلان منى بالشمال: إذا وصفتهما بالرفعة عندك والضعة، وذلك لتيمنهم بالميامن وتشاؤمهم بالشمائل،
Vol. 4, p. 457
and their taking the auspicious from the sānih «1» and ill omen from the bāriḥ; for that reason they derived the name for the right hand from yumn (blessing), and called the left hands “the ill-omened.” It is also said: the companions of the maymana and the companions of the mashʾama are the people of blessing and the people of ill omen, because the blessed are a blessing upon themselves by their obedience, and the wretched are an ill omen upon themselves by their disobedience. It is also said: the people of Paradise are taken to the right side and the people of the Fire to the left.
ولتفاؤلهم بالسانح «1» وتطيرهم من البارح، ولذلك اشتقوا لليمين الاسم من اليمن، وسموا الشمائل الشؤمى. وقيل: أصحاب الميمنة وأصحاب المشأمة: أصحاب اليمن والشؤم، لأنّ السعداء هيامين على أنفسهم بطاعتهم، والأشقياء مشائيم عليها بمعصيتهم. وقيل: يؤخذ بأهل الجنة ذات اليمين وبأهل النار ذات الشمال.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 456
1. (1) . A lion of ʿAthar hunts men, when
…. the lion shrinks from his peers, he is true. By Zuhayr, praising a brave man; he borrowed for him the name of the lion by explicit metaphor, and hunting is the embellishment. ʿAthar is the name of a place; that is, a brave man in ʿAthar who kills men when the mighty rider shrinks, that is, grows cowardly and weak toward his peers in battle — then he is true and his resolve is carried out and he kills his peer. In the verse is an antithesis between truthfulness and lying (ṣidq/kadhib), and it is among the beauties of speech.
2. . His statement «wa-futtitat until they become like groats»: the wording of al-Nasafī is: wa-futtitat (the intensive form). (ʿ)
3. . His statement «wa-fī kalām bint al-Khass»: in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: al-khass with fatḥa is a herb; al-khuss with ḍamma is the name of a man, and from it: Hind bint al-Khuss. ʿAyn hājja: that is, sunken. Al-ṣalā: what is on the right and left of the tail. Fajajtu mā bayna rijlayya afujjuhumā: when I spread them apart. One says: huwa yamshī mufājjan. (ʿ)
1. (1) . ليث يعثر يصطاد الرجال إذا
…. ما الليث كذب عن أقرانه صدقا لزهير يمدح شجاعا، فاستعار له اسم الأسد على طريق التصريحية، والاصطياد ترشيح. وعثر: اسم موضع، أى شجاع في عثر يقتل الرجال إذا كذب أى جبن وضعف الفارس الشديد عن أقرانه في الحرب، صدق هو ونفذ عزمه وقتل قرنه، وفي البيت الطباق بين الصدق والكذب، وهو من بديع الكلام.
2. . قوله «وفتت حتى تعود كالسويق» عبارة النسفي: وفتتت. (ع)
3. . قوله «وفي كلام بنت الخس» في الصحاح: الخس بالفتح: بقلة. والخس بالضم: اسم رجل. ومنه: هند بنت الخس. وعين هاجة: أى غائرة. والصلا: ما عن يمين الذنب ويساره. وفججت ما بين رجلي أفجهما: إذا فتحت. يقال: هو يمشى مفاجا. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 457
1. (1) . His statement «li-tafāʾulihim bi-l-sāniḥ»: it is what passes from your left to your right, of gazelle or bird. And al-bāriḥ is the opposite. Stated in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. (ʿ)
2. . Maḥmūd said: “‘What’ is an expression of wonder at the state of the two groups … etc.” Aḥmad said: He chose what is the preferred view, because it is more fitting to eloquence, but there remains to point out the difference between what is mentioned about the foremost and about the companions of the right, although in each of them only magnification and awe regarding the state of those mentioned is intended. So we say: the magnification conveyed by His saying “the foremost, the foremost” is more eloquent than its counterpart, because what this conveys is that the matter of the foremost and the greatness of their standing is hardly hidden, and it is only the bewilderment of the hearer's understanding about it that is well known. As for what is mentioned in His saying “And the companions of the right — what are the companions of the right?”, it is a magnification to the hearer of something of which he has no prior knowledge. Do you not see how the account of the state of the foremost came first, with His saying “those are the nearest,” joining the demonstrative pronoun, by which something known is indicated, with the predication about it by “the nearest,” defined with the alif-lām of familiarity? Nothing like this is mentioned in the exposition of the state of the companions of the right, for it is headed with His saying “amid thornless lote trees.”
1. (1) . قوله «لتفائلهم بالسانح» هو ما مر من يسارك إلى يمينك من ظبى أو طائر. والبارح: عكسه. أفاده الصحاح. (ع)
2. . قال محمود: «ما» تعجيب من حال الفريقين
…. الخ» قال أحمد: اختار ما هو المختار، لأنه أقعد بالفصاحة، لكن بقي التنبيه على المخالفة بين المذكورين في السابقين وفي أصحاب اليمين، مع أن كل واحد منهما إنما أريد به التعظيم والتهويل لحال المذكورين، فنقول: التعظيم المؤدى بقوله السَّابِقُونَ أبلغ من قرينه، وذلك أن مؤدى هذا: أن أمر السابقين وعظمة شأنه ما لا يكاد يخفى، وإنما تحير فهم السامع فيه مشهور. وأما المذكور في قوله فَأَصْحابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ ما أَصْحابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ فانه تعظيم على السامع بما ليس عنده منه علم سابق. ألا ترى كيف سبق بسط حال السابقين بقوله أُولئِكَ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ فجمع بين اسم الاشارة المشار به إلى معروف، وبين الاخبار عنه بقوله الْمُقَرَّبُونَ معرفا بالألف واللام العهدية، وليس مثل هذا مذكورا في بسط حال أصحاب اليمين، فانه مصدر بقوله فِي سِدْرٍ مَخْضُودٍ.
04
Q 56:10–26 · Vol. 4, pp. 457–460

Verses 10 to 26

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And the foremost, the foremost (10): those are the nearest (11), in the Gardens of Bliss (12). A multitude of the earlier ones (13) and a few of the later ones (14), on couches woven (with gold) (15), reclining on them, facing one another (16). Circulating among them will be immortal youths (17) with cups and pitchers and a goblet from a flowing spring (18), from which they get no headache nor are they intoxicated (19), and fruit of what they choose (20) and the flesh of fowl of what they desire (21), and wide-eyed maidens (22), like hidden pearls (23), as a reward for what they used to do (24). They will hear therein no idle talk nor sinful speech (25), but only the saying: Peace, peace (26)
وَالسَّابِقُونَ السَّابِقُونَ (10) أُولئِكَ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ (11) فِي جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ (12) ثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ (13) وَقَلِيلٌ مِنَ الْآخِرِينَ (14) عَلى سُرُرٍ مَوْضُونَةٍ (15) مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَيْها مُتَقابِلِينَ (16) يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ (17) بِأَكْوابٍ وَأَبارِيقَ وَكَأْسٍ مِنْ مَعِينٍ (18) لا يُصَدَّعُونَ عَنْها وَلا يُنْزِفُونَ (19) وَفاكِهَةٍ مِمَّا يَتَخَيَّرُونَ (20) وَلَحْمِ طَيْرٍ مِمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ (21) وَحُورٌ عِينٌ (22) كَأَمْثالِ اللُّؤْلُؤِ الْمَكْنُونِ (23) جَزاءً بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ (24) لا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيها لَغْواً وَلا تَأْثِيماً (25) إِلاَّ قِيلاً سَلاماً سَلاماً (26)
Vol. 4, p. 457
. “And the foremost” are the sincere ones who raced to what God called them to and split the dust in seeking the pleasure of God, mighty and majestic. It is also said: people are three: a man who was early to good in his youth and persisted in it until he departed from the world, so he is the foremost, the near; a man who began his life with sin and long heedlessness, then returned by repentance, so he is the companion of the right; and a man who was early to evil in his youth and did not cease from it until he departed from the world, so he is the companion of the left. “What are the companions of the right? What are the companions of the left?” is an expression of wonder at the state of the two groups in felicity and wretchedness «2».
وَالسَّابِقُونَ المخلصون الذين سبقوا إلى ما دعاهم الله إليه وشقوا الغبار في طلب مرضاة الله عز وجل وقيل: الناس ثلاثة فرجل ابتكر الخير في حداثة سنه، ثم داوم عليه حتى خرج من الدنيا، فهذا السابق المقرّب، ورجل ابتكر عمره بالذنب وطول الغفلة، ثم تراجع بتوبة، فهذا صاحب اليمين، ورجل ابتكر الشر في حداثة سنه، ثم يزل عليه حتى خرج من الدنيا، فهذا صاحب الشمال ما أصحاب الميمنة. ما أصحاب المشأمة؟ تعجيب من حال الفريقين في السعادة والشقاوة «2» .
Vol. 4, p. 458
And the meaning: what are they? “And the foremost, the foremost”: he means: and the foremost are those whose state you know and whose description has reached you, as in “ʿAbd Allāh is ʿAbd Allāh,” and the saying of Abū l-Najm: “and my poetry is my poetry” «1», as if he said: and my poetry is that which has reached you and which you have heard of its eloquence and mastery; and “the foremost” is made a corroboration, and “those are the nearest” a predicate, but that is not so. Some stopped at “and the foremost” and began “the foremost, those are the nearest”; but the correct view is to stop at the second, because it completes the sentence, and it corresponds to “what are the companions of the right” and “what are the companions of the left.” “The nearest, in the Gardens of Bliss”: those whose degrees are brought near to the Throne in Paradise and whose ranks are raised. It is also read fī jannati l-naʿīm. And thulla: a large community of people. He said: “And there came to them a Khindifite multitude … with an army like a foaming torrent” «2». And His saying, mighty and majestic, “and a few of the later ones” suffices as evidence of abundance; and it is from al-thall, which is breaking, just as umma is from amm, which is splitting the head, as if it were a group broken off from the people and cut from them. The meaning: the foremost among the earlier ones are many, and they are the nations from Adam ﷺ to Muḥammad ﷺ “and a few of the later ones,” who are the community of Muḥammad ﷺ. It is also said: “of the earlier ones” are those earlier in this community, and “of the later ones” are those later in it. From the Prophet ﷺ: “The two thirds all together are from my community” «3». If you ask: How did He say “and a few of the later ones,” then say “and a multitude of the later ones”?
والمعنى: أى شيء هم؟ والسابقون السابقون، يريد: والسابقون من عرفت حالهم وبلغك وصفهم، كقوله وعبد الله عبد الله. وقول أبى النجم: وشعري شعري «1» ، كأنه قال: وشعري ما انتهى إليك وسمعت بفصاحته وبراعته، وقد جعل السابقون تأكيدا. وأولئك المقرّبون: خبرا وليس بذاك. ووقف بعضهم على: والسابقون، وابتدأ السابقون أولئك المقرّبون، والصواب أن يوقف على الثاني، لأنه تمام الجملة، وهو في مقابلة: ما أصحاب الميمنة، وما أصحاب المشأمة الْمُقَرَّبُونَ فِي جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ الذين قربت درجاتهم في الجنة من العرش وأعليت مراتبهم. وقرئ: في جنة النعيم. والثلة: الأمة من الناس الكثيرة. قال: وجاءت إليهم ثلّة خندفيّة … بجيش كتيّار من السّيل مزبد «2» وقوله عز وجل وَقَلِيلٌ مِنَ الْآخِرِينَ كفى به دليلا على الكثرة، وهي من الثل وهو الكسر، كما أنّ الأمّة من الأمّ وهو الشج، كأنها جماعة كسرت من الناس وقطعت منهم. والمعنى: أنّ السابقين من الأوّلين كثير، وهم الأمم من لدن آدم عليه السلام إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وَقَلِيلٌ مِنَ الْآخِرِينَ وهم أمّة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم. وقيل مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ من متقدّمى هذه الأمة، ومِنَ الْآخِرِينَ من متأخريها. وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الثلثان جميعا من أمّتى» «3» . فإن قلت: كيف قال: وقليل من الآخرين، ثم قال: وَثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْآخِرِينَ؟
Vol. 4, p. 459
I answer: this is about the foremost and that is about the companions of the right, and they multiply from the earlier ones and the later ones all together.
قلت: هذا في السابقين وذلك في أصحاب اليمين، وأنهم يتكاثرون من الأولين والآخرين جميعا.
Question
If you ask: But it is reported that when it was revealed it was hard on the Muslims, and the Messenger of God ﷺ kept returning to his Lord until “a multitude of the earlier ones and a multitude of the later ones” was revealed.
فإن قلت: فقد روى أنها لما نزلت شق ذلك على المسلمين، فما زال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يراجع ربه حتى نزلت ثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ وَثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْآخِرِينَ.
Answer
I answer: this is not sound, for two reasons. One: this verse (the first) is clearly revealed about the foremost, and likewise the second is about the companions «1» of the right. Do you not see how He conjoined the companions of the right and His promise to them to the foremost and His promise to them? And the second: abrogation does not apply to reports. From al-Ḥasan ؓ: the foremost of the nations are more than the foremost of our community, and the followers of the nations are like the followers of this community. “Thulla” is the predicate of an omitted subject, that is: they are a multitude. “Mawḍūna”: plaited with gold «2», interlaced with pearls and rubies, some of it interwoven with the other, as the rings of mail are woven. Al-Aʿshā said: “and from the weaving of David, woven” «3». It is also said: continuous, some of it brought near some. “Reclining”: a circumstantial from the pronoun in ʿalā, which is its governor, that is: they settled upon them reclining; “facing one another”: none looks at the backs of the necks of others. They were described with good fellowship and refinement of manners and etiquette. “Mukhalladūn”: kept forever in the form of youths and the stage of wuṣāfa «4», not changing from it. It is also said: wearing earrings, al-khalada being the earring. It is also said: they are the children of the people of this world, who had no good deeds to be rewarded for, nor evil deeds to be punished for. It is reported from ʿAlī ؓ and from al-Ḥasan. And in the hadith: “The children of the unbelievers are the servants of the people of Paradise” «5». The akwāb: vessels without handles and spouts,
قلت: هذا لا يصح لأمرين، أحدهما: أنّ هذه الآية واردة في السابقين ورودا ظاهرا، وكذلك الثانية في أصحاب «1» اليمين. ألا ترى كيف عطف أصحاب اليمين ووعدهم، على السابقين ووعدهم، والثاني: أنّ النسخ في الأخبار غير جائز. وعن الحسن رضى الله عنه: سابقو الأمم أكثر من سابقي أمّتنا، وتابعو الأمم مثل تابعي هذه الأمّة. وثلة: خبر مبتدإ محذوف، أى: هم ثلة مَوْضُونَةٍ مرمولة بالذهب، «2» مشبكة بالدرّ والياقوت، قد دوخل بعضها في بعض كما توضن حلق الدرع. قال الأعشى: ومن نسج داود موضونة «3» وقيل: متواصلة، أدنى بعضها من بعض. مُتَّكِئِينَ حال من الضمير في على، وهو العامل فيها، أى: استقرّوا عليها متكئين مُتَقابِلِينَ لا ينظر بعضهم في أقفاء بعض. وصفوا بحسن العشرة وتهذيب الأخلاق والآداب مُخَلَّدُونَ مبقون أبدا على شكل الولدان وحدّ الوصافة، «4» لا يتحوّلون عنه. وقيل: مقرّطون، والخلدة: القرط. وقيل: هم أولاد أهل الدنيا: لم تكن لهم حسنات فيثابوا عليها، ولا سيئات فيعاقبوا عليها. روى عن على رضى الله عنه وعن الحسن. وفي الحديث: «أولاد الكفار خدّام أهل الجنة» «5» . الأكواب: أوان بلا عرى وخراطيم،
Vol. 4, p. 460
and pitchers, those with spouts. “Lā yuṣaddaʿūna ʿanhā”: that is, because of it; its reality: their headache does not issue from it. Or: they are not split away from it. Mujāhid read lā yaṣdaʿūna, meaning they do not split apart, are not dispersed, as in “on that day they will be split apart,” and yaṣdaʿūna, that is, some of them do not split others, do not disperse them. “Yatakhayyarūna”: they take its best and choicest. “Yashtahūna”: they wish for. It is also read wa-luḥūmi ṭayr. It is read wa-ḥūrun ʿīn in the nominative, meaning: and in it are wide-eyed maidens, like the verse of Sībawayh: “except for stationary (hearth-stones), their embers ash … and a split one …” «1».. or by conjunction upon “youths”; and in the genitive: by conjunction upon “Gardens of Bliss,” as if He said: they are in the Gardens of Bliss, and in fruit, meat and wide-eyed maidens; or upon “cups,” because the meaning of “immortal youths circulate among them with cups” is that they enjoy cups; and in the accusative: and they will be given wide-eyed maidens. “Jazāʾan” is an object of purpose, that is: all that is done to them as a reward for their deeds. “Salāman salāman” is either a substitute for “qīlan,” by the evidence of His saying “they will hear therein no idle talk except peace,” or an object of “qīlan,” meaning: they will hear therein nothing except that they say “Peace, peace.” The meaning: they spread greeting among them, greeting one another peace after peace. It is also read salāmun salāmun, as a quotation.
والأباريق، ذوات الخراطيم لا يُصَدَّعُونَ عَنْها أى بسببها، وحقيقته: لا يصدر صداعهم عنها. أو لا يفرّقون عنها. وقرأ مجاهد: لا يصدعون، بمعنى: لا يتصدعون لا يتفرقون، كقوله يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصَّدَّعُونَ ويصدعون، أى: لا يصدع بعضهم بعضا، لا يفرّقونهم يَتَخَيَّرُونَ يأخذون خيره وأفضله يَشْتَهُونَ يتمنون. وقرئ: ولحوم طير. قرئ: وحور عين، بالرفع على: وفيها حور عين، كبيت الكتاب: إلّا رواكد جمرهنّ هباء … ومشجّج.......... «1» .. أو للعطف على ولدان، وبالجر: عطفا على جنات النعيم، كأنه قال: هم في جنات النعيم، وفاكهة ولحم وحور. أو على أكواب، لأن معنى يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ بِأَكْوابٍ ينعمون بأكواب، وبالنصب على: ويؤتون حورا جَزاءً مفعول له، أى: يفعل بهم ذلك كله جزاء بأعمالهم سَلاماً سَلاماً إما بدل من قِيلًا بدليل قوله لا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيها لَغْواً إِلَّا سَلاماً وإما مفعول به لقيلا، بمعنى: لا يسمعون فيها إلا أن يقولوا سلاما سلاما. والمعنى: أنهم يفشون السلام بينهم، فيسلمون سلاما بعد سلام. وقرئ سلام سلام، على الحكاية.
Editor’s notes on these 4 pages
Vol. 4, p. 457
1. (1) . His statement «li-tafāʾulihim bi-l-sāniḥ»: it is what passes from your left to your right, of gazelle or bird. And al-bāriḥ is the opposite. Stated in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. (ʿ)
2. . Maḥmūd said: “‘What’ is an expression of wonder at the state of the two groups … etc.” Aḥmad said: He chose what is the preferred view, because it is more fitting to eloquence, but there remains to point out the difference between what is mentioned about the foremost and about the companions of the right, although in each of them only magnification and awe regarding the state of those mentioned is intended. So we say: the magnification conveyed by His saying “the foremost, the foremost” is more eloquent than its counterpart, because what this conveys is that the matter of the foremost and the greatness of their standing is hardly hidden, and it is only the bewilderment of the hearer's understanding about it that is well known. As for what is mentioned in His saying “And the companions of the right — what are the companions of the right?”, it is a magnification to the hearer of something of which he has no prior knowledge. Do you not see how the account of the state of the foremost came first, with His saying “those are the nearest,” joining the demonstrative pronoun, by which something known is indicated, with the predication about it by “the nearest,” defined with the alif-lām of familiarity? Nothing like this is mentioned in the exposition of the state of the companions of the right, for it is headed with His saying “amid thornless lote trees.”
1. (1) . قوله «لتفائلهم بالسانح» هو ما مر من يسارك إلى يمينك من ظبى أو طائر. والبارح: عكسه. أفاده الصحاح. (ع)
2. . قال محمود: «ما» تعجيب من حال الفريقين
…. الخ» قال أحمد: اختار ما هو المختار، لأنه أقعد بالفصاحة، لكن بقي التنبيه على المخالفة بين المذكورين في السابقين وفي أصحاب اليمين، مع أن كل واحد منهما إنما أريد به التعظيم والتهويل لحال المذكورين، فنقول: التعظيم المؤدى بقوله السَّابِقُونَ أبلغ من قرينه، وذلك أن مؤدى هذا: أن أمر السابقين وعظمة شأنه ما لا يكاد يخفى، وإنما تحير فهم السامع فيه مشهور. وأما المذكور في قوله فَأَصْحابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ ما أَصْحابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ فانه تعظيم على السامع بما ليس عنده منه علم سابق. ألا ترى كيف سبق بسط حال السابقين بقوله أُولئِكَ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ فجمع بين اسم الاشارة المشار به إلى معروف، وبين الاخبار عنه بقوله الْمُقَرَّبُونَ معرفا بالألف واللام العهدية، وليس مثل هذا مذكورا في بسط حال أصحاب اليمين، فانه مصدر بقوله فِي سِدْرٍ مَخْضُودٍ.
Vol. 4, p. 458
1. (1) . I am Abū l-Najm and my poetry is my poetry
…. How excellent my work, what my breast conceals! My eye sleeps while my heart journeys by night
…. with the ghouls in a barren land. By Abū l-Najm al-ʿIjlī. He means: I am the one known for eloquence among people, like a famous proper name. And my poetry is the eloquent one known to be the poetry of Abū l-Najm, for when the subject and predicate, or the condition and the apodosis, are the same, the speech indicates exaggeration of magnification or of belittlement. The present case is of the first kind, by the evidence of the context. In it is a claim that the utmost greatness is in the man called Abū l-Najm and the utmost eloquence in the poetry attributed to him. Al-darr is milk, but what is meant by it is work and making, that is: to God belongs my making, meaning that it is great. Janna l-layl: it grew dark. [Janna] al-nabt: it grew long and tangled. [Janna] al-dhubāb: its buzzing grew loud. Jannahu l-layl: it concealed it; ajannahu l-ṣadr: the breast hid it. Mā is exclamatory. Ajanna is a verb of wonder, that is: something great made my breast encompass strange meanings; it is possible that mā is a substitute for darr, and ajanna a past verb serving as a relative clause or description of it. Fu'ādī: my heart or my mind. Yasrā: travels by night; that is, my thought spends the night as if going with the ghouls in an open land without vegetation, because of its distance in meanings. And the second verse is an explanation of the first.
2. . And there came to them a Khindifite multitude
…. with an army like a foaming torrent. He says: a group of people came to them attributed to Khindif, the wife of Ilyās b. Muḍar. His saying “with an army” is of the type of tajrīd, as if he extracted from the multitude another army, to exaggerate abundance. It is possible that the bāʾ means “with” or “in,” because the army is wider than the multitude; and it is from jāsha when it moves and surges, as if boiling. Al-tayyār: swiftly flowing water, and min is explanatory or partitive. And al-mazbid: that whose foam rises on its surface through its abundance and its surging.
3. . Reported by al-Ṭabarī and Ibn ʿAdī from the narration of Abān from Saʿīd b. Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said regarding this verse “a multitude of the earlier ones and a multitude of the later ones”: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Both are from my community.” Abān is Ibn Abī ʿAyyāsh, abandoned (matrūk). Isḥāq reported it, with his chain to al-Ṭayālisī, and Ibrāhīm al-Ḥarbī and al-Ṭabarānī, from the narration of Zayd b. Ṣuhbān from Abū Bakra, as raised and as halted; and the halted is more likely correct. And ʿAlī is weak.
1. (1) . أنا أبو النجم وشعري شعري
…. لله درى ما أجن صدري تنام عينى وفؤادي يسرى
…. مع العفاريت بأرض قفر لأبى النجم العجلى. يريد: أنا المعروف بالبلاغة بين الناس كالعلم المشهور. وشعري: هو البليغ المعروف بأنه شعر أبى النجم، لأنه إذا اتحد المبتدأ والخبر أو الشرط والحزاء: دل الكلام على المبالغة في التعظيم أو في التحقير. وما هنا من الأول بدليل السياق. وفيه ادعاء أن نهاية العظمة في الرجل المسمى بأبى النجم، ونهاية البلاغة في الشعر المنسوب إليه. والدر: اللبن، لكن المراد به العمل والصنع، أى: لله صنيعي، يعنى: أنه عظيم. وجن الليل: أظلم. والنبت: طال والتف. والذباب: كثرت أصواته. وجنه الليل: ستره، وأجنه الصدر: أكنه. وما تعجبية. وأجن: فعل تعجب، أى: شيء عظيم جعل صدري محيطا بالمعاني الغريبة، ويحتمل أن «ما» يدل من درى. وأجن: فعل ماض صلة أو صفة له، ومؤادى: قلبي أو عقلى. يسرى: يسير ليلا. أى: يبيت فكرى كأنه ذاهب مع العفاريت بأرض فضاء لا نبات بها، لا بعاده في المعاني. والبيت الثاني بيان للأول.
2. . وجاءت إليهم ثلة خندفية
…. بحيش كتيار من السيل مزيد يقول: وجاءت اليهم جماعة من الناس منسوبة إلى خندف امرأة إلياس بن مضر. وقوله «يجيش» من باب التجريد، كأنه انتزع من الثلة جيشا غيرها مبالغة في الكثرة. ويحتمل أن الباء بمعنى مع، أو في، لان الجيش أوسع من الثلة، وهو من جاش إذا تحرك واضطرب، كأنه يغلى، والتيار: الماء الشديد الجري، ومن بيانية أو تبعيضية. والمزيد: المرتفع زبده على وجهه لكثرته وفوراته.
3. . أخرجه الطبري وابن عدى من رواية أبان عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال في هذه الآية ثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ وَثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْآخِرِينَ قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «هما جميعا من أمتى» وأبان هو ابن أبى عياش متروك. ورواه إسحاق وسنده إلى الطيالسي وإبراهيم الحربي والطبراني من رواية زيد بن صهبان عن أبى بكرة مرفوعا وموقوفا. والموقوف أولى بالصواب. وعلى ضعيف.
Vol. 4, p. 459
1. (1) . His statement «wa-kadhālika l-thāniya fī aṣḥāb al-yamīn»: that is, its coming is clearly stated. (ʿ) [.....]
2. . His statement «marmūla bi-l-dhahab»: in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: ramaltu l-ḥaṣīr, that is, I wove it (saffaftuhu). And in it also: saffaftu l-khūṣ: that is, I plaited it. (ʿ)
3. . And from the weaving of David, woven
…. driven along with the tribe, band after band. By al-Aʿshā, describing coats of mail, and he made them the weaving of our master David to exaggerate the excellence of their craft, because he wove them by God's command and instruction to him. Mawḍūna: that is, some of it inserted into some, so they are tightly woven, to be driven, that is: their owners with the tribe. Al-ʿayr with fatḥa: the chief, that is, chief after chief, brought up; and al-ʿayr is also applied to a bird that flies above a traveling caravan, but that is unlikely to be intended here.
4. . His statement «wa-ḥadd al-waṣāfa»: it is the boy's reaching the age of service. Stated in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. (ʿ)
5. . Reported by al-Bazzār and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ from the narration of ʿAbbād b. Manṣūr from Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī from Samura b. Jundab, who said: “We asked the Messenger of God ﷺ about the children of the polytheists, and he said: they are the servants of the people of Paradise.” Al-Bazzār also reported it from the narration of ʿAlī b. Zayd b. Judʿān, and al-Ṭayālisī, al-Ṭabarānī and Abū Yaʿlā from the narration of Yazīd al-Raqāshī, both from Anas, with this and more fully. I say: it may be contradicted by the hadith of Samura in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, in which he saw the children of people beneath a tree, with Abraham ﷺ caring for them. He said: we said, And the children of the polytheists? He said: “And the children of the polytheists.” He reported it with this wording. It is possible to reconcile the two, since there is no conflict between them, for they may be so in the intermediate realm (barzakh), and then after settling they settle in Paradise as servants of its people.
1. (1) . قوله «وكذلك الثانية في أصحاب اليمين» أى ظاهرة الورود. (ع) [.....]
2. . قوله «مرمولة بالذهب» في الصحاح: رملت الحصير، أى: سففته. وفيه أيضا: سففت الخوص: أى نسجته. (ع)
3. . ومن نسج داود موضونة
…. تساق مع الحي عيرا فعيرا للأعشى، يصف الدروع، وجعلها من نسج سيدنا داود مبالغة في حسن صنعتها، لأنه نسجها بأمر من الله وتعليمه له. موضونة: أى مدخل بعضها في بعض، فهي محكمة النسج لتساق، أى: أصحابها مع الحي. والعير بالفتح: السيد، أى سيدا بعد سيد متربين، ويطلق العير على طائر يطير فوق القافلة السائرة، وتبعد إرادته هنا.
4. . قوله «وحد الوصافة» هي بلوغ الغلام حد الخدمة. أفاده الصحاح. (ع)
5. . أخرجه البزار والطبراني في الأوسط من رواية عباد بن منصور عن أبى رجاء العطاردي عن سمرة بن جندب قال «سألنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أولاد المشركين فقال هم خدم أهل الجنة» ورواه البزار من براية على بن زيد بن جدعان والطيالسي والطبراني وأبو يعلى من رواية يزيد الرقاشي كلاهما عن أنس بهذا وأتم منه قلت: قد يعارضه حديث سمرة في صحيح البخاري. فقيه أنه رأى أولاد الناس تحت شجرة يكفلهم إبراهيم عليه السلام قال فقلنا: وأولاد المشركين؟ قال: وأولاد المشركين» أخرجه بهذا اللفظ. ويمكن الجمع بينهما بأن لا منافاة بينهما لاحتمال أن يكونوا في البرزخ كذلك، ثم بعد الاستقرار يستقرون في الجنة خدما لأهلها.
Vol. 4, p. 460
1. (1) . They perished, and their traces were altered with decay,
…. except for stationary ones, their embers ashes, and a split one, either the middle of its top
…. appeared, and its remnant, al-Mughrāʾ, was altered. By al-Shammākh, and it is said: by Dhū l-Rumma, and it is among the verses of al-Kitāb. Bāda yabīdu: perished. Al-āy: a collective noun for āya, which is a sign. Al-rawākid: the hearth-stones (athāfī), which are the stones on which the pot is placed. Al-habāʾ: ashes mixed with dust. Al-mushajjaj: an adjective that has come to function as a noun, for the tent-peg whose head was split by pounding, so that around its head fringes appear resembling the qadhāl, which is the hair of the sides of the head. Sawāʾ al-shayʾ: its middle. It is also narrated ghayyaba instead of ghayyara. Al-sār, with hamza or without it: the remainder. Al-Mughrāʾ: a land whose soil is mixed with stones and pebbles. He says: the abodes perished for you and their traces were worn away, and nothing remained but the place of the fire and the remnant of the tent-peg. It is also narrated rawākida in the accusative, so the nominative is conjoined to the accusative relying on the meaning.
1. (1) . بادت وغير آيهن مع البلى
…. إلا رواكد جمرهن هباء ومشجج إما سواء قذاله
…. فبدا وغير ساره المغراء الشماخ، وقيل: لذي الرمة، وهي من أبيات الكتاب. وباد يبيد: هلك يهلك. والآي: اسم جمع آية وهي علامة والرواكد: الأثافى. وهي الأحجار التي توضع عليها للقدر. والهباء: الرماد المختلط بالتراب. والمشجج: صفة جرت مجرى الاسم لوتد الخباء الذي تشجح رأسه من الدق. فبرز حول رأسه أطراف تشبه القذال، وهو شعر جوانب الرأس. وسواء الشيء. وسطه. ويروى: غيب، بدل: غير. والسار بالهمز وتركه: البقية. والمغراء: أرض يخالط ترابها حجارة وحصى، يقول هلكت لك الديار وبليت آثارها، ولم يبق إلا محل النار وبقية وتد الخباء. ويروى: رواكد بالنصب، فعطف المرفوع على المنصوب اعتمادا على المعنى.
05
Q 56:27–40 · Vol. 4, pp. 460–462

Verses 27 to 40

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And the companions of the right — what are the companions of the right (27)? Amid thornless lote trees (28) and clustered banana trees (29) and extended shade (30) and poured-out water (31) and abundant fruit (32), neither cut off nor forbidden (33), and raised couches (34). Indeed We have produced them in a [new] production (35) and made them virgins (36), loving, of equal age (37), for the companions of the right (38): a multitude of the earlier ones (39) and a multitude of the later ones (40)
وَأَصْحابُ الْيَمِينِ ما أَصْحابُ الْيَمِينِ (27) فِي سِدْرٍ مَخْضُودٍ (28) وَطَلْحٍ مَنْضُودٍ (29) وَظِلٍّ مَمْدُودٍ (30) وَماءٍ مَسْكُوبٍ (31) وَفاكِهَةٍ كَثِيرَةٍ (32) لا مَقْطُوعَةٍ وَلا مَمْنُوعَةٍ (33) وَفُرُشٍ مَرْفُوعَةٍ (34) إِنَّا أَنْشَأْناهُنَّ إِنْشاءً (35) فَجَعَلْناهُنَّ أَبْكاراً (36) عُرُباً أَتْراباً (37) لِأَصْحابِ الْيَمِينِ (38) ثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ (39) وَثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْآخِرِينَ (40)
Vol. 4, p. 461
Al-sidr: the lote tree (nabiq). “Al-makhḍūd”: that without thorns, as if its thorns were cut off «1». From Mujāhid: the laden, whose branches are bent by the abundance of its fruit, from khaḍada l-ghuṣn when one bent it while moist. “Al-ṭalḥ”: the banana tree. It is also said: it is the umm ghaylān tree, which has abundant sweet-smelling blossom. From al-Suddī: a tree resembling the ṭalḥ of the world, but it has fruit sweeter than honey. From ʿAlī ؓ: that he read wa-ṭalʿ, [saying] “what business has the ṭalḥ?” «2», and he recited «3» His saying “its spathe is layered”; so it was said to him: Shall we change it? He said: The verses of the Qurʾān are not disturbed today nor changed. And from Ibn ʿAbbās something similar. “Al-manḍūd”: that which is piled «4» with fruit from its bottom to its top, so it has no bare trunk. “And extended shade”: stretching, spread out, not shrinking, like the shade between the rising of dawn and the rising of the sun. “Maskūb”: poured for them wherever and however they wish, with no toil in it. It is also said: ever-flowing, never interrupted. It is also said: poured out, running on the earth without a channel. “Neither cut off”: it is perpetual, not cut off at some times like the fruits of the world; “nor forbidden”: not withheld from whoever reaches for it in any way, and not prohibited as the orchards of the world are prohibited. It is read wa-fākihatun kathīra in the nominative, meaning: and there is fruit, as in “ḥūrun ʿīn.” “Furush”: plural of firāsh. It is also read wa-furush in the lighter form. “Raised”: piled until it rose; or raised upon the couches. It is also said: they are women, because a woman is alluded to as a bed (firāsh); raised upon the couches. God the Exalted said “They and their spouses will be in shade, reclining on couches,” and His saying “Indeed We have produced them in a [new] production” indicates this. On the first interpretation He implied “for them,” because the mention of the furush, which are resting-places, indicated them. “We produced them”: We began their creation anew without birth; so either those whose production was begun, or those whose production was repeated, is meant. From the Messenger of God ﷺ «5»: that Umm Salama ؓ asked him about God the Exalted's saying “Indeed We have produced them,” and he said: O Umm Salama,
السدر: شجر النبق. والمخضود: الذي لا شوك له، كأنما خضد شوكه «1» . وعن مجاهد: الموقر الذي تثنى أغصانه كثرة حمله، من خضد الغصن إذا ثناء وهو رطب. والطلح: شجر الموز. وقيل: هو شجر أم غيلان، وله نوار كثير طيب الرائحة. وعن السدى: شجر يشبه طلح الدنيا، ولكن له ثمر أحلى من العسل. وعن على رضى الله عنه أنه قرأ: وطلع، وما شأن الطلح، «2» وقرأ «3» قوله لَها طَلْعٌ نَضِيدٌ فقيل له: أو نحوّلها؟ فقال: آي القرآن لا تهاج اليوم ولا تحوّل. وعن ابن عباس نحوه. والمنضود: الذي نضد «4» بالحمل من أسفله إلى أعلاه، فليست له ساق بارزة وَظِلٍّ مَمْدُودٍ ممتدّ منبسط لا يتقلص، كظلّ ما بين طلوع الفجر وطلوع الشمس مَسْكُوبٍ يسكب لهم أين شاءوا وكيف شاءوا لا يتعنون فيه. وقيل: دائم الجرية لا ينقطع. وقيل: مصبوب يجرى على الأرض في غير أخدود لا مَقْطُوعَةٍ هي دائمة لا تنقطع في بعض الأوقات كفواكه الدنيا وَلا مَمْنُوعَةٍ لا تمنع عن متناولها بوجه، ولا يحظر عليها كما يحظر على بساتين الدنيا. وقرئ: وفاكهة كثيرة، بالرفع على: وهناك فاكهة، كقوله: وحور عين وَفُرُشٍ جمع فراش. وقرئ: وفرش، بالتخفيف مَرْفُوعَةٍ نضدت حتى ارتفعت. أو مرفوعة على الأسرة. وقيل: هي النساء، لأن المرأة يكنى عنها بالفراش مرفوعة على الأرائك. قال الله تعالى هُمْ وَأَزْواجُهُمْ فِي ظِلالٍ عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ مُتَّكِؤُنَ، ويدل عليه قوله تعالى إِنَّا أَنْشَأْناهُنَّ إِنْشاءً وعلى التفسير الأول أضمر لهنّ، لأنّ ذكر الفرش وهي المضاجع دلّ عليهن أَنْشَأْناهُنَّ إِنْشاءً أى ابتدأنا خلقهن ابتداء جديدا من غير ولادة، فإما أن يراد. اللاتي ابتدئ إنشاؤهن، أو اللاتي أعيد إنشاؤهن. وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «5» . أنّ أمّ سلمة رضى الله عنها سألته عن قوله الله تعالى. إِنَّا أَنْشَأْناهُنَّ فقال: يا أم سلمة
Vol. 4, p. 462
they are those who were taken in the abode of the world as old women, gray-haired, bleary-eyed «1»; God made them [so] after old age.” “Atrāban”: of one birth, in evenness «2»; whenever their husbands come to them they find them virgins. When ʿĀʾisha ؓ heard that from the Messenger of God ﷺ she said: Oh, my pain! The Messenger of God ﷺ said: There is no pain there. An old woman said to the Messenger of God ﷺ: Pray to God that He admit me to Paradise. He said: Old women do not enter Paradise. So she turned away weeping, and he, peace and blessings upon him, said: “Tell her that on that day she will not be old” «3», and he recited the verse. “ʿUruban”: it is also read ʿurban, lightened, plural of ʿarūb, the one who endears herself to her husband and is fair in her conduct as a wife. “Atrāban”: equal in age, daughters of thirty-three, and their husbands too likewise. From the Messenger of God ﷺ: “The people of Paradise will enter Paradise hairless, beardless, fair, curly-haired, kohl-eyed, sons of thirty-three” «4». And the lām in “for the companions of the right” belongs to “We produced” and “We made.”
هنّ اللواتي قبضن في دار الدنيا عجائز شمطاء رمصاء «1» ، جعلهنّ الله بعد الكبر» أَتْراباً على ميلاد واحد في الاستواء «2» ، كلما أتاهنّ أزواجهنّ وجدوهنّ أبكارا، فلما سمعت عائشة رضى الله عنها ذلك من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت: وأوجعاه فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ليس هناك وجع. وقالت عجوز لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ادع الله أن يدخلني الجنة، لقال: إنّ الجنة لا تدخلها العجائز، فولت وهي تبكى، فقال عليه الصلاة السلام: «أخبروها أنها ليست يومئذ بعجوز» «3» وقرأ الآية عُرُباً وقرئ: عربا، بالتخفيف جمع عروب وهي المتحببة إلى زوجها الحسنة التبعل أَتْراباً مستويات في السن بنات ثلاث وثلاثين، وأزواجهنّ أيضا كذلك. وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يدخل أهل الجنة الجنة جردا مردا بيضا جعادا مكحلين أبناء ثلاث وثلاثين» «4» واللام في لِأَصْحابِ الْيَمِينِ من صلة أنشأنا وجعلنا.

Vol. 4, p. 461
1. (1) . His statement «ka-annamā khuḍida shawkuhu»: in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: khaḍadtu l-shajar: I cut off its thorns; and khaḍadtu l-ʿūd, that is, I bent it without breaking. (ʿ)
2. . His statement «wa-mā shaʾn al-ṭalḥ»: perhaps: and he said: what business has the ṭalḥ? (ʿ)
3. . His statement «wa-qaraʾa»: that is, as evidence for his reading. (ʿ)
4. . His statement «wa-l-manḍūd alladhī nuḍida»: in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: it is that which is stacked, some of it over some. (ʿ)
5. . Al-Thaʿlabī reported it in full from the path of al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlawiyya al-Qaṭṭān from Ismāʿīl b. ʿĪsā from al-Musayyab b. Sharīk, mentioning it, and he did not raise [to the Prophet] anything except the story of ʿĀʾisha. And from the path of Ghunjār, Ismāʿīl b. Abī l-Bād related to us from Yūnus from al-Ḥasan from Umm Salama as raised, without the story of ʿĀʾisha. Al-Ṭabarī, al-Ṭabarānī and Ibn Mardawayh reported from the path of ʿUmar b. Hāshim al-Bayrūtī from Sulaymān b. Abī Karīma from Hishām from al-Ḥasan from his mother from Umm Salama, who said: I said, O Messenger of God, tell me about God's saying “loving, of equal age” — and he mentioned it. And in it: “So He made them virgins, loving, endeared and beloved to their husbands, of equal age, of one birth.” Al-Tirmidhī reported part of it from the path of Mūsā b. ʿUbayda from Yazīd al-Raqāshī and considered it weak.
1. (1) . قوله «كأنما خضد شوكه» في الصحاح «خضدت الشجر» قطعت شوكه، وخضدت العود، أى: ثنيته من غير كسر. (ع)
2. . قوله «وما شأن الطلح» لعله: وقال ما شأن الطلح. (ع)
3. . قوله «وقرأ» أى: استشهادا على قراءته. (ع)
4. . قوله «والمنضود الذي نضد» في الصحاح: أنه المرصوص بعضه فوق بعض. (ع)
5. . أخرجه الثعلبي بتمامه من طريق الحسن بن علوية القطان عن إسماعيل بن عيسى عن المسيب بن شريك فذكره ولم يرفع إلا قصة عائشة. ومن طريق غنجار حدثنا إسماعيل بن أبى الباد عن يونس عن الحسن عن أم سلمة مرفوعا دون قصة عائشة. وروى الطبري والطبراني وابن مردويه من طريق عمر بن هاشم البيروتى عن سليمان بن أبى كريمة عن هشام عن الحسن عن أمه عن أم سلمة قالت: قلت يا رسول الله، أخبرنى عن قوله تعالى عُرُباً أَتْراباً فذكره. وفيه «فجعلهن عذارى عربا متعشقات متحببات إلى أزواجهن، أترابا على ميلاد واحد» وروى الترمذي من طريق موسى بن عبيدة عن يزيد الزقاش طرفا منه واستضعفه.
Vol. 4, p. 462
1. (1) . His statement «ʿajāʾiz shamṭāʾ ramṣā»: in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: al-shamṭ is the whiteness of the hair of the head mixed with its blackness; the man is ashmaṭ and the woman shamṭāʾ. And in it: al-ramaṣ is filth that gathers in the corner of the eye; raṃiṣat ʿaynuhu, and the man is armaṣ — that is, and the woman ramṣāʾ — and the plural is shumṭ and rumṣ. (ʿ)
2. . His statement «mīlād wāḥid fī l-istiwāʾ»: perhaps it is connected with the meaning of comparison, that is: as if they were of one birth in evenness of creation. (ʿ)
3. . Al-Tirmidhī reported it in al-Shamāʾil from the narration of Mubārak b. Fuḍāla from al-Ḥasan, as mursal, and his wording is fuller. It has other chains. Among them, in al-Baʿth, al-Bayhaqī from the narration of Layth b. Abī Sulaym from Mujāhid from ʿĀʾisha. And among them, in al-Awsaṭ, from the narration of Masʿada b. al-Yasaʿ from Saʿīd from Qatāda from Saʿīd b. al-Musayyab from ʿĀʾisha. And Khārija b. Muṣʿab reported it from Saʿīd from Qatāda from Anas. All of them are weak.
4. . Aḥmad, Ibn Abī Shayba, Abū Yaʿlā and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ reported it from the narration of Ḥammād b. Salama from ʿAlī b. Zayd from Saʿīd b. al-Musayyab from Abū Hurayra with this; and he added: “upon the creation of Adam, sixty cubits, seven cubits in width.” Ibn Abī Ḥātim mentioned in al-ʿIlal that his father said: Abū Salama reported it from Ḥammād as mursal and did not mention Abū Hurayra in it; and so Ibn Saʿd reported it from Yaḥyā b. al-Sakan from Ḥammād. And ʿAlī b. Zayd is weak. On this topic [there is a report] from Muʿādh b. Jabal. Al-Tirmidhī reported it and said: gharīb. Some of Qatāda's companions sent it as mursal. Al-Bayhaqī reported it connected, then reported it halted at Qatāda. [.....]
1. (1) . قوله «عجائز شمطاء رمصا» في الصحاح «الشمط» : بياض شعر الرأس يخالط سواده، والرجل أشمط، والمرأة شمطاء. وفيه: الرمص: وسخ يجتمع في الموق، وقد رمصت عينه، والرجل أرمص اه، أى: والمرأة رمصاء، والجمع شمط ورمص. (ع)
2. . قوله «ميلاد واحد في الاستواء» لعله متعلق بمعنى التشبيه، أى: كأنهن على ميلاد واحد في استواء الخلق. (ع)
3. . أخرجه الترمذي في الشمائل من رواية مبارك بن فضالة عن الحسن بهذا مرسلا وسياقه أتم. وله طرق أخرى. منها في البعث البيهقي من رواية ليث بن أبى سليم عن مجاهد عن عائشة. ومنها في الأوسط من رواية مسعدة ابن اليسع عن سعيد عن قتادة عن سعيد بن المسيب عن عائشة. ورواه خارجة بن مصعب عن سعيد عن قتادة عن أنس. وكلها ضعيفة.
4. . أخرجه أحمد وابن أبى شبية وأبو يعلى والطبراني في الأوسط من رواية حماد بن سلمة عن على بن زيد عن سعيد بن المسيب عن أبى هريرة بهذا. وزاد على خلق آدم ستون ذراعا عرض سبعة أذرع. وذكر ابن أبى حاتم في العلل أن أباه قال: رواه أبو سلمة عن حماد مرسلا ولم يذكر فيه أبا هريرة وكذا أخرجه ابن سعد عن يحيى بن السكن عن حماد. وعلى بن زيد ضعيف. وفي الباب عن معاذ بن جبل. أخرجه الترمذي وقال: غريب. وبعض أصحاب قتادة أرسلوه. وأخرجه البيهقي موصولا، ثم أخرجه موقوفا على قتادة. [.....]
06
Q 56:41–56 · Vol. 4, pp. 462–464

Verses 41 to 56

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And the companions of the left — what are the companions of the left (41)? In scorching wind and boiling water (42) and a shade of black smoke (43), neither cool nor generous (44). Indeed they were, before that, affluent (45) and used to persist in the great sin (46) and used to say: When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected (47), and our forefathers too (48)? Say: Indeed the earlier ones and the later ones (49) will surely be gathered for the appointed time of a known day (50). Then indeed you, O astray ones, deniers (51), will surely eat from a tree of zaqqūm (52) and fill your bellies with it (53) and drink on top of it of boiling water (54), drinking like thirst-stricken camels (55). This is their hospitality on the Day of Judgment (56)
وَأَصْحابُ الشِّمالِ ما أَصْحابُ الشِّمالِ (41) فِي سَمُومٍ وَحَمِيمٍ (42) وَظِلٍّ مِنْ يَحْمُومٍ (43) لا بارِدٍ وَلا كَرِيمٍ (44) إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا قَبْلَ ذلِكَ مُتْرَفِينَ (45) وَكانُوا يُصِرُّونَ عَلَى الْحِنْثِ الْعَظِيمِ (46) وَكانُوا يَقُولُونَ أَإِذا مِتْنا وَكُنَّا تُراباً وَعِظاماً أَإِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ (47) أَوَآباؤُنَا الْأَوَّلُونَ (48) قُلْ إِنَّ الْأَوَّلِينَ وَالْآخِرِينَ (49) لَمَجْمُوعُونَ إِلى مِيقاتِ يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ (50) ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ أَيُّهَا الضَّالُّونَ الْمُكَذِّبُونَ (51) لَآكِلُونَ مِنْ شَجَرٍ مِنْ زَقُّومٍ (52) فَمالِؤُنَ مِنْهَا الْبُطُونَ (53) فَشارِبُونَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْحَمِيمِ (54) فَشارِبُونَ شُرْبَ الْهِيمِ (55) هذا نُزُلُهُمْ يَوْمَ الدِّينِ (56)
Vol. 4, p. 463
“In samūm”: in the heat of a fire that penetrates the pores; “and ḥamīm”: boiling water, extremely hot; “and a shade of yaḥmūm”: of dark, pitch-black smoke; “neither cool nor generous”: a negation of two attributes of shade from it. He means: it is a shade, but not like other shades; he called it a shade, then negated from it the coolness of shade and its comfort and its benefit to whoever takes shelter in it from the harm of heat — and that is its generosity (karam) — to obliterate what in the signification of “shade” is of seeking relief in it. The meaning: it is a hot, harmful shade, except that negation in such cases has a force that affirmation does not. And in it is mockery of the companions of the left, that they are not worthy of the cool, generous shade that belongs to their opposites in Paradise. It is also read lā bāridun wa-lā karīm in the nominative, that is: it is not so. “Al-ḥinth”: the great sin. From it their saying: the boy reached al-ḥinth, that is, puberty and the age of being held accountable for sins. From it: ḥanitha fī yamīnihi, the opposite of barra in it. And one says taḥannatha when he abstains from sin and keeps away from it. “Awa-ābāʾunā”: the interrogative hamza entered upon the conjunctive particle.
فِي سَمُومٍ في حر نار ينفذ في المسام وَحَمِيمٍ وماء حار متناه في الحرارة وَظِلٍّ مِنْ يَحْمُومٍ من دخان أسود بهيم لا بارِدٍ وَلا كَرِيمٍ نفى لصفتى الظل عنه، يريد: أنه ظل، ولكن لا كسائر الظلال: سماه ظلا، ثم نفى عنه برد الظل وروحه ونفعه لمن يأوى إليه من أذى الحر وذلك كرمه ليمحق ما في مدلول الظل من الاسترواح إليه. والمعنى أنه ظل حارّ ضارّ إلا أنّ للنفي في نحو هذا شأنا ليس للإثبات. وفيه تهكم بأصحاب الشأمة، وأنهم لا يستأهلون الظل البارد الكريم الذي هو لأضدادهم في الجنة. وقرئ: لا بارد ولا كريم بالرفع، أى: لا هو كذلك والْحِنْثِ الذنب العظيم. ومنه قولهم: بلغ الغلام الحنث، أى: الحلم ووقت المؤاخذة بالمآثم. ومنه: حنث في يمينه، خلاف: برّ فيها. ويقال: تحنث إذا تأثم وتحرج أَوَآباؤُنَا دخلت همزة الاستفهام على حرف العطف.
Question
If you ask: How is conjunction upon the hidden pronoun in “la-mabʿūthūn” good without a corroboration by “naḥnu”?
فإن قلت: كيف حسن العطف على المضمر في لَمَبْعُوثُونَ من غير تأكيد بنحن؟
Answer
I answer: it is good because of the separator, which is the hamza, as it was good in His saying “we did not associate, nor did our fathers,” because of the separation by the lā that corroborates the negation. It is also read aw ābāʾunā. It is also read la-mujmaʿūn «1» “to the appointed time of a known day”: to that by which the world was timed, a known day; and the genitive construction means min, like “a ring of silver.” And al-mīqāt is that by which a thing is timed, that is, delimited. From it the mawāqīt of iḥrām: they are the limits which one who wishes to enter Mecca may not pass except in iḥrām. “O you astray ones” from guidance, “deniers” of the resurrection, who are the people of Mecca and those in a similar state. “From a tree, of zaqqūm”: the first min is for the beginning of the range, and the second is for explaining the tree and interpreting it. And he made the pronoun of the tree feminine according to the meaning, and masculine according to the wording in His saying “minhā” and “ʿalayhi”; and whoever reads “min shajarin min zaqqūmin” has made both pronouns for the tree, and the second is masculine only on the interpretation of zaqqūm, because it explains it and it is in its meaning. “Shurba l-hīm”: it is read with the three vowels; the fatḥa and ḍamma are verbal nouns. From Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq ؓ: “days of eating and drinking,” with fatḥa on the shīn. As for the kasra, it means the thing drunk, that is, what the hīm drink, which are camels afflicted with hiyām, a disease from which they drink and are not quenched; plural of ahyam and haymāʾ. Dhū l-Rumma said:
قلت: حسن للفاصل الذي هو الهمزة، كما حسن في قوله تعالى ما أَشْرَكْنا وَلا آباؤُنا لفصل لا المؤكدة النفي. وقرئ: أو آباؤنا. وقرئ: لمجمعون «1» إِلى مِيقاتِ يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ إلى ما وقتت به الدنيا من يوم معلوم، والإضافة بمعنى من، كخاتم فضة. والميقات: ما وقت به الشيء، أى: حدّ. ومنه مواقيت الإحرام: وهي الحدود التي لا يتجاوزها من يريد دخول مكة إلا محرما أَيُّهَا الضَّالُّونَ عن الهدى الْمُكَذِّبُونَ بالبعث، وهم أهل مكة ومن في مثل حالهم مِنْ شَجَرٍ مِنْ زَقُّومٍ من الأولى لابتداء الغاية، والثانية لبيان الشجر وتفسيره. وأنث ضمير الشجر على المعنى، وذكره على اللفظ في قوله مِنْهَا وعَلَيْهِ ومن قرأ مِنْ شَجَرٍ مِنْ زَقُّومٍ فقد جعل الضميرين للشجرة، وإنما ذكر الثاني على تأويل الزقوم، لأنه تفسيرها وهي في معناه شُرْبَ الْهِيمِ قرئ بالحركات الثلاث، فالفتح والضم: مصدران. وعن جعفر الصادق رضى الله عنه، أيام أكل وشرب، بفتح الشين. وأما المكسور فبمعنى المشروب، أى: ما يشربه الهيم وهي الإبل التي بها الهيام، وهو داء تشرب منه فلا تروى: جمع أهيم وهيماء. قال ذو الرمّة:
Vol. 4, p. 464
“So I became like the thirsty camel (hīmāʾ), the water does not cool her thirst, nor does her hiyām finish her off” «1». It is also said that al-hīm are the sands. Its explanation is that it is the plural of al-hiyām with fatḥa on the hāʾ, which is loose sand that does not hold together, pluralized on the pattern fuʿul like saḥāb and suḥub, then lightened and done to it what is done to the plural of abyaḍ. The meaning: such hunger is let loose upon them as forces them to eat the zaqqūm, which is like molten brass; and when they fill their bellies with it, such thirst is let loose upon them as forces them to drink the boiling water that cuts their intestines, so they drink it like the drinking of the hīm.
فأصبحت كالهيماء لا الماء مبرد … صداها ولا يقضى عليها هيامها «1» وقيل الهيم: الرمال. ووجهه أن يكون جمع الهيام بفتح الهاء وهو الرمل الذي لا يتماسك، جمع على فعل كسحاب وسحب، ثم خفف وفعل به ما فعل بجمع أبيض. والمعنى: أنه يسلط عليهم من الجوع ما يضطرّهم إلى أكل الزقوم الذي هو كالمهل، فإذا ملؤوا منه البطون يسلط عليهم من العطش ما يضطرّهم إلى شرب الحميم الذي يقطع أمعاءهم، فيشربونه شرب الهيم.
Question
If you ask: How is the conjunction of the two drinkers upon the two drinkers sound, when they are for the same persons and are two identical attributes, so that it would be the conjunction of a thing upon itself?
فإن قلت: كيف صحّ عطف الشاربين على الشاربين، وهما لذوات متفقة، وصفتان متفقتان، فكان عطفا للشيء على نفسه؟
Answer
I answer: they are not identical, in that their being drinkers of the boiling water as it is, with its extreme heat and cutting of intestines, is a marvelous matter, and their drinking it so, as the hīm drink water, is also a marvelous matter, so they are two different attributes. “Al-nuzul”: the provision prepared for the guest in honor of him. And in it is mockery, as in His saying “so give them tidings of a painful punishment,” and as in the saying of Abū l-Shaʿr al-Ḍabbī: “And when the tyrant came to us with an army as a guest, we made the spears and the thin swords his hospitality” «2». It is also read nuzlahum, lightened.
قلت: ليسنا بمتفقتين، من حيث إنّ كونهم شاربين للحميم على ما هو عليه: من تناهى الحرارة وقطع الأمعاء: أمر عجيب، وشربهم له على ذلك كما تشرب الهيم الماء: أمر عجيب أيضا، فكانتا صفتين مختلفتين. النزل: الرزق الذي يعدّ للنازل تكرما له. وفيه تهكم، كما في قوله تعالى فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ وكقول أبى الشعر الضبي. وكنّا إذا الجبّار بالجيش ضافنا … جعلنا القنا والموهفات له نزلا «2» وقرئ: نزلهم بالتخفيف.
Editor’s notes on these 3 pages
Vol. 4, p. 462
1. (1) . His statement «ʿajāʾiz shamṭāʾ ramṣā»: in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: al-shamṭ is the whiteness of the hair of the head mixed with its blackness; the man is ashmaṭ and the woman shamṭāʾ. And in it: al-ramaṣ is filth that gathers in the corner of the eye; raṃiṣat ʿaynuhu, and the man is armaṣ — that is, and the woman ramṣāʾ — and the plural is shumṭ and rumṣ. (ʿ)
2. . His statement «mīlād wāḥid fī l-istiwāʾ»: perhaps it is connected with the meaning of comparison, that is: as if they were of one birth in evenness of creation. (ʿ)
3. . Al-Tirmidhī reported it in al-Shamāʾil from the narration of Mubārak b. Fuḍāla from al-Ḥasan, as mursal, and his wording is fuller. It has other chains. Among them, in al-Baʿth, al-Bayhaqī from the narration of Layth b. Abī Sulaym from Mujāhid from ʿĀʾisha. And among them, in al-Awsaṭ, from the narration of Masʿada b. al-Yasaʿ from Saʿīd from Qatāda from Saʿīd b. al-Musayyab from ʿĀʾisha. And Khārija b. Muṣʿab reported it from Saʿīd from Qatāda from Anas. All of them are weak.
4. . Aḥmad, Ibn Abī Shayba, Abū Yaʿlā and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ reported it from the narration of Ḥammād b. Salama from ʿAlī b. Zayd from Saʿīd b. al-Musayyab from Abū Hurayra with this; and he added: “upon the creation of Adam, sixty cubits, seven cubits in width.” Ibn Abī Ḥātim mentioned in al-ʿIlal that his father said: Abū Salama reported it from Ḥammād as mursal and did not mention Abū Hurayra in it; and so Ibn Saʿd reported it from Yaḥyā b. al-Sakan from Ḥammād. And ʿAlī b. Zayd is weak. On this topic [there is a report] from Muʿādh b. Jabal. Al-Tirmidhī reported it and said: gharīb. Some of Qatāda's companions sent it as mursal. Al-Bayhaqī reported it connected, then reported it halted at Qatāda. [.....]

[.....]
Vol. 4, p. 463
1. (1) . His statement «and it is read la-mujmaʿūn ilā mīqāt»: in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: ajmaʿtu l-shayʾ: I made it whole (jamīʿan). (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «وقرئ: لمجمعون إلى ميقات» في الصحاح: أجمعت الشيء: جعلته جميعا. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 464
1. (1) . And Mayy had provisioned us, despite the distance, with a kiss,
…. links of needs whose sickness is long. So I became like the thirsty camel, the water does not cool
…. her thirst, nor does her hiyām finish her off. By Dhū l-Rumma. He says: she provisioned us, that is, Mayy made our provision at departure a kiss, and the kiss was the links of needs and causes of yearning for union; so ʿalāqāt is a nominative predicate, or an accusative substitute. Al-suqām like kalām, and saqam like taʿab, and saqam like bukhl: the verbal noun of saqima like taʿiba taʿaban, that is: its affliction is of long duration and does not heal. It is said of a male camel ahyam and of a she-camel haymāʾ, when afflicted by al-hiyām with ḍamma: a disease from which camels' hearts boil like severe thirst; that is: so I became like the thirsty she-camel. And his saying “the water does not cool” is a new clause explaining the point of likeness in her, or a circumstantial clause from her: that is, water does not cool her thirst and does not finish her off, that is, her hiyām does not kill her; so I am likewise: there is no union to heal me, nor does the yearning kill me. It is also narrated: wa-lā yuqḍā ʿalā hiyāmihā, and perhaps its meaning is: the water does not cool the burning that I got from her, nor does the hiyām that I got from her kill me; but the first is more fitting and better in meaning.
2. . The explanation of this witness verse was given in part one, page 458; consult it if you wish. — its corrector.
1. (1) . وقد زودت مى على النأى قبلة
…. علاقات حاجات طويل سقامها فأصبحت كالهيماء لا الماء مبرد
…. صداها ولا يقضى عليها هيامها لذي الرمة، يقول: وقد زودتنا، أى جعلت زادنا مى عند الرحيل قبلة، فكانت القبلة علاقات الحاجات وأسباب التطلع إلى الوصال، فعلاقات: خبر مرفوع، أو بدل منصوب. والسقام ككلام، وسقم كتعب، وسقم كبخل: مصدر سقم كتعب تعبا، أى: عناؤها طويل المدة لا يبرأ. ويقال للجمل: أهيم. وللناقة هيماء، إذا أصابهما الهيام بالضم: وهو داء تغلى منه قلوب الإبل كالعطش الشديد، أى: فأصبحت كالناقة الهيماء. وقوله «لا الماء مبرد» استئناف مبين لوجه الشبه فيها. أو حال منها، أى: لا يبرد الماء ظمأها ولا يقضى عليها، أى: لا يمينها هيامها، فأنا كذلك لا وصال فيشفينى، ولا التلهف يميتني. ويروى: ولا يقضى على هيامها، ولعل معناه: لا الماء يبرد الحرقة التي حصلت لي منها، ولا يميتني الهيام الذي حصل لي منها، ولكن الأولى أقعد وأجود معنى.
2. . تقدم شرح هذا الشاهد بالجزء الأول صفحة 458 فراجعه إن شئت اه مصححه.
07
Q 56:57–62 · Vol. 4, pp. 464–465

Verses 57 to 62

The verses as the commentary quotes them
We created you, so why do you not believe (57)? Have you seen what you emit (58)? Is it you who create it, or are We the Creator (59)? We have decreed death among you, and We are not outstripped (60) in that We may change your likenesses and produce you in what you do not know (61). And you have already known the first creation, so why do you not remember (62)
نَحْنُ خَلَقْناكُمْ فَلَوْلا تُصَدِّقُونَ (57) أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ ما تُمْنُونَ (58) أَأَنْتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُ أَمْ نَحْنُ الْخالِقُونَ (59) نَحْنُ قَدَّرْنا بَيْنَكُمُ الْمَوْتَ وَما نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ (60) عَلى أَنْ نُبَدِّلَ أَمْثالَكُمْ وَنُنْشِئَكُمْ فِي ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ (61) وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ النَّشْأَةَ الْأُولى فَلَوْلا تَذَكَّرُونَ (62)
Vol. 4, p. 464
?
Vol. 4, p. 465
“So why do you not believe?” is an urging to believe: either in the creation, because although they believe in it, since their doctrine is contrary to what belief entails, they are as if denying it; or in the resurrection, because one who created first cannot be prevented from creating a second time. “What you emit” is what you eject, that is, what you cast into the wombs of sperm-drops. Abū l-Summāl read it with fatḥa on the tāʾ; one says amnā l-nuṭfa and manāhā. God the Exalted said “from a sperm-drop when emitted.” “Takhluqūnahu”: you determine and shape it. “We have decreed death among you”: a decree, and We apportioned it among you as provision is apportioned, with variation and disparity as Our will requires, so your lifespans differ, short, long and middling. It is also read qaddarnā, lightened. Sabaqtuhu ʿalā l-shayʾ: when you make him unable to reach it and overcome him in it and do not let him have it. So the meaning of His saying “and We are not outstripped in that We may change your likenesses” is that We are able to do that and you will not overcome Us in it; and amthālakum is the plural of mithl: that is, that We replace you, and in your place, with likenesses of you among creation, and that We produce you in a creation you do not know and have no acquaintance with the like of it — meaning that We are able to do both: to create what resembles you and what does not resemble you; so how could We be unable to bring you back? It is also possible that amthālakum is the plural of mathal, that is, that We replace and change your attributes in which you are in your creation and your characters, and produce you in attributes you do not know. It is read al-nashʾa and al-nashāʾa. And in this is evidence for the soundness of analogical reasoning (qiyās), since He called them ignorant for leaving analogy of the later creation upon the first.
فَلَوْلا تُصَدِّقُونَ تحضيض على التصديق: إما بالخلق لأنهم وإن كانوا مصدّقين به، إلا أنهم لما كان مذهبهم خلاف ما يقتضيه التصديق، فكأنهم مكذبون به. وإما بالبعث، لأنّ من خلق أولا لم يمتنع عليه أن يخلق ثانيا ما تُمْنُونَ ما تمنونه، أى: تقذفونه في الأرحام من النطف. وقرأ أبو السمال بفتح التاء، يقال: أمنى النطفة ومناها. قال الله تعالى مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ إِذا تُمْنى. تَخْلُقُونَهُ تقدرونه وتصوّرونه قَدَّرْنا بَيْنَكُمُ الْمَوْتَ تقديرا وقسمناه عليكم قسمة الرزق على اختلاف وتفاوت كما تقتضيه مشيئتنا، فاختلفت أعماركم من قصير وطويل ومتوسط. وقرئ: قدرنا بالتخفيف. سبقته على الشيء: إذا أعجزته عنه وغلبته عليه ولم تمكنه منه، فمعنى قوله وَما نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ عَلى أَنْ نُبَدِّلَ أَمْثالَكُمْ أنا قادرون على ذلك لا تغلبوننا عليه، وأمثالكم جمع مثل: أى على أن نبدل منكم ومكانكم أشباهكم من الخلق، وعلى أن نُنْشِئَكُمْ في خلق لا تعلمونها وما عهدتم بمثلها، يعنى: أنا نقدر على الأمرين جميعا: على خلق ما يماثلكم، وما لا يماثلكم، فكيف نعجز عن إعادتكم. ويجوز أن يكون أَمْثالَكُمْ جمع مثل، أى: على أن نبدل ونغير صفاتكم التي أنتم عليها في خلقكم وأخلاقكم، وننشئكم في صفات لا تعلمونها. قرئ النشأة والنشاءة. وفي هذا دليل على صحة القياس حيث جهّلهم في ترك قياس النشأة الأخرى على الأولى.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 464
1. (1) . And Mayy had provisioned us, despite the distance, with a kiss,
…. links of needs whose sickness is long. So I became like the thirsty camel, the water does not cool
…. her thirst, nor does her hiyām finish her off. By Dhū l-Rumma. He says: she provisioned us, that is, Mayy made our provision at departure a kiss, and the kiss was the links of needs and causes of yearning for union; so ʿalāqāt is a nominative predicate, or an accusative substitute. Al-suqām like kalām, and saqam like taʿab, and saqam like bukhl: the verbal noun of saqima like taʿiba taʿaban, that is: its affliction is of long duration and does not heal. It is said of a male camel ahyam and of a she-camel haymāʾ, when afflicted by al-hiyām with ḍamma: a disease from which camels' hearts boil like severe thirst; that is: so I became like the thirsty she-camel. And his saying “the water does not cool” is a new clause explaining the point of likeness in her, or a circumstantial clause from her: that is, water does not cool her thirst and does not finish her off, that is, her hiyām does not kill her; so I am likewise: there is no union to heal me, nor does the yearning kill me. It is also narrated: wa-lā yuqḍā ʿalā hiyāmihā, and perhaps its meaning is: the water does not cool the burning that I got from her, nor does the hiyām that I got from her kill me; but the first is more fitting and better in meaning.
2. . The explanation of this witness verse was given in part one, page 458; consult it if you wish. — its corrector.
1. (1) . وقد زودت مى على النأى قبلة
…. علاقات حاجات طويل سقامها فأصبحت كالهيماء لا الماء مبرد
…. صداها ولا يقضى عليها هيامها لذي الرمة، يقول: وقد زودتنا، أى جعلت زادنا مى عند الرحيل قبلة، فكانت القبلة علاقات الحاجات وأسباب التطلع إلى الوصال، فعلاقات: خبر مرفوع، أو بدل منصوب. والسقام ككلام، وسقم كتعب، وسقم كبخل: مصدر سقم كتعب تعبا، أى: عناؤها طويل المدة لا يبرأ. ويقال للجمل: أهيم. وللناقة هيماء، إذا أصابهما الهيام بالضم: وهو داء تغلى منه قلوب الإبل كالعطش الشديد، أى: فأصبحت كالناقة الهيماء. وقوله «لا الماء مبرد» استئناف مبين لوجه الشبه فيها. أو حال منها، أى: لا يبرد الماء ظمأها ولا يقضى عليها، أى: لا يمينها هيامها، فأنا كذلك لا وصال فيشفينى، ولا التلهف يميتني. ويروى: ولا يقضى على هيامها، ولعل معناه: لا الماء يبرد الحرقة التي حصلت لي منها، ولا يميتني الهيام الذي حصل لي منها، ولكن الأولى أقعد وأجود معنى.
2. . تقدم شرح هذا الشاهد بالجزء الأول صفحة 458 فراجعه إن شئت اه مصححه.

His statement «Abū Hurayra said: a-raʾaytum»: that is, he cited the verse as evidence for the hadith, which is His saying “Have you seen what you till?”; and his saying “a-raʾaytum” is addressed to the one who hears from him; he meant the sense of looking, so he made it transitive with ilā, as in His saying “Have they not looked at what God has created of anything” (a-wa-lam yaraw ilā mā khalaqa llāhu min shayʾ). Q 56:63–67 · Vol. 4, pp. 465–466

Verses 63 to 67

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Have you seen what you till (63)? Is it you who make it grow, or are We the Grower (64)? If We willed, We would make it debris, and you would be left marveling (65): “We are indeed burdened with debt (66); rather, we are deprived (67)
أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ ما تَحْرُثُونَ (63) أَأَنْتُمْ تَزْرَعُونَهُ أَمْ نَحْنُ الزَّارِعُونَ (64) لَوْ نَشاءُ لَجَعَلْناهُ حُطاماً فَظَلْتُمْ تَفَكَّهُونَ (65) إِنَّا لَمُغْرَمُونَ (66) بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ (67)
Vol. 4, p. 465
.” “Have you seen what you till” of food, that is: you sow its grain and work its land; “is it you who make it grow” — cause it to sprout and turn it into a plant, flourishing and growing «1» until it reaches its end. From the Messenger of God ﷺ: “Let none of you say: I sowed (zaraʿtu); let him say: I tilled (ḥaraththu)” «2». Abū Hurayra said: Have you considered «3» His saying:
أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ ما تَحْرُثُونَ من الطعام، أى: تبذرون حبه وتعملون في أرضه أَأَنْتُمْ تَزْرَعُونَهُ تنبتونه وتردونه نباتا، يرف وينمى «1» إلى أن يبلغ الغاية. وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا يقولن أحدكم: زرعت، وليقل: حرثت» «2» قال أبو هريرة: أرأيتم إلى «3» قوله:
Vol. 4, p. 466
“Have you seen …” the verse. And al-ḥuṭām is from ḥaṭama, like al-futāt and al-judhādh from fatta and jadhdha: that which has become crushed and broken. “Fa-ẓaltum”: it is also read with kasra, and fa-ẓalaltum in the original form. “Tafakkahūn”: you marvel. From al-Ḥasan ؓ: you regret your toil in it and your spending on it; or over the sins you committed on account of which you were afflicted with that. It is also read tafakkanūn. From it the hadith: “The likeness of the scholar is like the spring (ḥamma) to which the distant come «1» and which those near abandon; while they were so, its water sank; some people benefited from it and some remained regretting (yatafakkanūn)” «2», that is, regretting. “We are indeed burdened with debt”: bound to the penalty of what we spent, and ruined by the ruin of our provision, from al-gharām, which is destruction. “Rather we are deprived”: a people deprived (maḥrūmūn), unlucky and denied good fortune, with no portion and no luck for us; had we been fortunate, this would not have befallen us. It is also read a-innā.
أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ … الآية. والحطام: من حطم، كالفتات والجذاذ من فت وجذ: وهو ما صار هشيما وتحطم فَظَلْتُمْ وقرئ بالكسر. وفظللتم على الأصل تَفَكَّهُونَ تعجبون. وعن الحسن رضى الله عنه: تندمون على تعبكم فيه وإنفاقكم عليه. أو على ما اقترفتم من المعاصي التي أصبتم يذلك من أجلها. وقرئ: تفكنون. ومنه الحديث «مثل العالم كمثل الحمة يأتيها البعداء «1» ويتركها القرباء فبيناهم إذ غار ماؤها فانتفع بها قوم وبقي قوم يتفكنون» «2» أى: يتندمون إِنَّا لَمُغْرَمُونَ لملزمون غرامة ما أنفقنا. ومهلكون لهلاك رزقنا، من الغرام: وهو الهلاك بَلْ نَحْنُ قوم مَحْرُومُونَ محارفون محدودون، لاحظ لنا ولا بخت لنا، ولو كنا مجدودين، لما جرى علينا هذا. وقرئ: أئنا.

Q 56:68–70 · Vol. 4, pp. 466–467

Verses 68 to 70

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Have you seen the water you drink (68)? Is it you who sent it down from the rain clouds, or are We the Sender (69)? If We willed, We would make it salty; so why do you not give thanks (70)
أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ الْماءَ الَّذِي تَشْرَبُونَ (68) أَأَنْتُمْ أَنْزَلْتُمُوهُ مِنَ الْمُزْنِ أَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنْزِلُونَ (69) لَوْ نَشاءُ جَعَلْناهُ أُجاجاً فَلَوْلا تَشْكُرُونَ (70)
Vol. 4, p. 466
? “The water you drink”: he means: the sweet water fit for drinking. “Al-muzn”: the clouds, the singular being muzna. It is also said: it is specifically the white cloud, and it is the sweetest water. “Ujājan”: salty, brackish «3», impossible to drink.
الْماءَ الَّذِي تَشْرَبُونَ يريد: الماء العذب الصالح للشرب. والْمُزْنِ السحاب: الواحدة مزنة. وقيل: هو السحاب الأبيض خاصة، وهو أعذب ماء أُجاجاً ملحا زعاقا «3» لا يقدر على شربه.
Question
If you ask: Why was the lām introduced into the apodosis of “law” in His saying “la-jaʿalnāhu ḥuṭāman” and removed from it here?
فإن قلت: لم أدخلت اللام على جواب لَوْ في قوله لَجَعَلْناهُ حُطاماً ونزعت منه هاهنا؟
Answer
I answer: since “law” is applied to two sentences, the second of which is made to depend on the first as the apodosis depends on the condition, and it is not exclusively conditional like “in” nor does it act like it, but the sense of condition entered it incidentally in so far as it indicates in the content of its two sentences that the second was impossible because of the impossibility of the first, it needed in its apodosis something that raises a mark of this dependence; so this lām was added to be a mark of that. And if it is omitted after having become a well-known mark in its place, it is because a thing, once it has become a mark and its position is well known and it has become familiar and customary, one does not mind dropping it from the utterance, relying on the hearer's knowledge. Do you not see what is told of Ruʾba, that he used to say “Khayr” to one who said to him “How are you this morning?” — he omitted the preposition because everyone knew its place; and the states of its omission and its inclusion are equal because of its fame. And enough for you is the saying of Aws: “until when the hunting dogs, he said to them: / ‘Like today — one pursued, or one pursuing!’” «4»
قلت: إنّ «لو» لما كانت داخلة على جملتين معلقة ثانيتهما بالأولى تعلق الجزاء بالشرط، ولم تكن مخلصة للشرط كإن ولا عاملة مثلها، وإنما سرى فيها معنى الشرط اتفاقا من حيث إفادتها في مضمونى جملتيها أنّ الثاني امتنع لامتناع الأوّل: افتقرت في جوابها إلى ما ينصب علما على هذا التعلق، فزيدت هذه اللام لتكون علما على ذلك، فإذا حذفت بعد ما صارت علما مشهورا مكانه، فلأن الشيء إذا علم وشهر موقعه وصار مألوفا ومأنوسا به: لم يبال بإسقاطه عن اللفظ، استغناء بمعرفة السامع. ألا ترى إلى ما يحكى عن رؤبة أنه كان يقول: خير، لمن قال له: كيف أصبحت؟ فحذف الجار لعلم كل أحد بمكانه. وتساوى حالى حذفه وإثباته لشهرة أمره. وناهيك بقول أوس: حتى إذا الكلّاب قال لها … كاليوم مطلوبا ولا طلبا «4»
Vol. 4, p. 467
and his omission of “lam ara” (I have not seen); so its omission is a verbal abbreviation while it is present in meaning; the two places are equal without difference between them, besides which the earlier mention of it, with the distance short, suffices for mentioning it a second time and substitutes for it. It may also be said that this lām gives the meaning of emphasis without doubt, so it was introduced in the verse of what is eaten and not in the verse of what is drunk, to indicate that the matter of what is eaten takes precedence over the matter of what is drunk, and that the threat of its loss is harsher and more severe, since what is drunk is needed only as a follower of what is eaten. Do you not see that you give your guest drink only after feeding him; and if you reversed it, you would fall under the saying of Abū l-ʿAlāʾ: “When people's guests are given pure milk to drink, they give their guests cold, sweet water” «1». And one of the Arabs was given a drink and said: I do not drink except upon a thumayla (a remnant of food in the stomach); and for this reason the verse of what is eaten was put before the verse of what is drunk.
وحذفه «لم أر» فإذن حذفها اختصار لفظي وهي ثابتة في المعنى، فاستوى الموضعان بلا فرق بينهما، على أن تقدّم ذكرها والمسافة قصيرة مغن عن ذكرها ثانية ونائب عنه. ويجوز أن يقال: إنّ هذه اللام مفيدة معنى التوكيد لا محالة، فأدخلت في آية المطعوم دون آية المشروب، للدلالة على أن أمر المطعوم مقدّم على أمر المشروب، وأن الوعيد بفقده أشد وأصعب، من قبل أن المشروب إنما يحتاج إليه تبعا للمطعوم. ألا ترى أنك إنما تسقى ضيفك بعد أن تطعمه، ولو عكست قعدت تحت قول أبى العلاء: إذا سقيت ضيوف النّاس محضا … سقوا أضيافهم شبما زلالا «1» وسقى بعض العرب فقال: أنا لا أشرب إلا على ثميلة، ولهذا قدّمت آية المطعوم على آية المشروب.

1. (1) . قوله «كمثل الحمة يأتيها البعداء» في الصحاح «الحمة» : العين الحارة يستشفى بها الأعلاء والمرضى. وفي الحديث: «العالم كالحمة» اه. (ع)

Al-makhḍ — with two dotted letters — is milk with its butter removed, so it is in the sense of mamkhūḍ. It is also narrated maḥḍan, with the undotted ḥāʾ, that is: pure, sweet or sour. Al-shabim — like ḥadhir — is cold. Al-zulāl: [printed: “al-ʿaqib”]. That said, since the scholars of rhetoric give the context a role in indicating what is intended, we say: the meaning of the verse is: when people hasten milk for their guests and content themselves with it instead of hastening the food, they [the praised ones] hasten food for their guests because of their readiness for guests, so [the guests] need to drink water, and so they give them water to drink before others feed their guests; so their giving them water to drink conveys the hastening of food before it, with the assistance of the context, because it customarily entails it, so there is no fault in it.

(1) . لأبى العلاء يمدح سعد الدولة أبا الفضائل، وعيب عليه حيث مدح بسقى الضيوف الماء قبل ذكر الطعام. والمخض- بمعجمتين-: اللبن المنزوع زبده، فهو بمعنى الممخوض. ويروى: محضا، بالحاء المهملة، أى: خالصا حلوا أو حامضا. والشبم- كحذر-: البارد. والزلال: العقب. هذا وحيث جعل علماء البلاغة للمقام مدخلا في الدلالة على المراد فنقول: إن معنى البيت: إذا عجلت الناس اللبن لأضيافهم واكتفوا به عن الاسراع بالطعام: عجلوا هم بالطعام لضيوفهم لاستعدادهم للضيفان، فيحتاجون لشرب الماء، فيسقونهم ماء قبل إطعام غيرهم الضيفان، فسقيهم الماء يفيد تعجيل الطعام قبله بمعونة المقام، لأنه يلزمه عادة فلا عيب فيه.
